subject: Implementation checklist and gating for SSO/SCIM + per-tenant IP allowlists
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@globex.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@globex.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Implementation checklist and gating for SSO/SCIM + per-tenant IP allowlists

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for working with us on the Globex pilot. To help the implementation team prepare, I attached a compact checklist and sketched the gating decisions we typically surface during onboarding. Key asks for this week:

- Confirm IdP metadata (SAML 2.0 metadata XML) or a staging Okta org we can hit.
- Confirm whether SCIM provisioning should be scoped to a dedicated service account (recommended) and whether Globex wants full CRUD or just user create/patch.
- Provide the per-tenant outbound IP ranges (CIDR) that need to be allowlisted; also indicate if those ranges are static or NAT'ed behind your edge.
- Any org policies we need to enforce up front (e.g., require MFA for admin role, SCIM deprovision TTL).

I've proposed a 30-minute sync on Thursday to walk the team through the checklist and agree on a deployment gating plan (SSO smoke tests, SCIM dry-run, IP allowlist cutover). Proposed times in the attached calendar stub.

Attachments: implementation-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll loop in CS engineering after your answers so we can map the service account scopes and rollout cadence.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@globex.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@globex.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Implementation checklist and gating for SSO/SCIM + per-tenant IP allowlists

Thanks Tessa — good checklist. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- IdP: Globex is on Okta; we can export the SAML metadata XML and share it with your team.
- SCIM: We prefer a dedicated service account for provisioning. For the pilot, we only need create and patch (no deletes from SCIM, we handle lifecycle on our side).
- IP ranges: attaching a PDF with our firewall team's notes — most outbound egress is through two NAT pools; they may change during a planned network refresh next quarter.
- Org policies: we require admin MFA and a 7-day deprovision hold before disabling an account (so we can validate audit windows).

I attached a short document with the firewall notes and our internal security contact. We can commit to the Thursday slot at 10:00 AM ET if that works for the Redwood team.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Cloud Identity & Access
Globex Corporation

Attachments: globex-scim-requirements.pdf

Date: 2025-10-07T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation checklist and gating for SSO/SCIM + per-tenant IP allowlists

Elena — great, thanks for the quick confirmations and the firewall notes. Confirming the Thursday 10:00 AM ET slot — I booked the session and invited your security contact.

Two clarifications from our side before the sync: 
1) SCIM scope: Ben, our implementation lead, recommends a token with "scim:users:write" and "scim:users:read" only (no delete). We will not perform delete operations unless Globex explicitly opts in after pilot signoff.
2) IP allowlist workflow: if your egress ranges are going to change during the network refresh, we should plan a short maintenance window where we switch the allowlist to the new CIDRs and perform smoke tests. If change is frequent, we can propose using a short-lived VPN or a bastion IP during the cutover to avoid repeated rule churn.

Ben / Monica — can you confirm the recommended service-account token TTL and whether KMS-encrypted secrets are required for the provisioning account? Also flag any rate-limit or batching considerations for SCIM syncs in the pilot (we want to avoid throttling when you run a large user import).

Thanks,
Tessa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@globex.com>
Date: 2025-10-08T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation checklist and gating for SSO/SCIM + per-tenant IP allowlists

Hi all — jumping in with implementation specifics so the Thursday sync is productive. Notes below are what our infra and security teams will implement for the pilot unless Globex asks to adjust: 

- SCIM token & scopes: provide a long-lived token for the pilot with scopes: scim.users:read, scim.users:write. TTL: 90 days recommended for pilot; rotate on signoff. If Globex requires KMS-backed secrets, we will accept and fetch via your KMS endpoint during sync. (Attachment: scim-scope-snippet.txt)

- Service account pattern: one dedicated service account per environment (staging, prod). For pilot, staging-only service account is fine; production will require least-privilege and RBAC mapping to your groups.

- IP allowlist cutover: because Globex’s NAT pools may change next quarter, recommended approach is: (1) use temporary bastion IPs for initial traffic; (2) coordinate a 30-min maintenance window for allowlist swap; (3) run automated smoke tests (token exchange, SAML Assertion test, sample SCIM upsert). We can produce a short-runbook for the switch. (Attachment: ip-allowlist-template.csv)

- Rate limiting & batching: if you import >10k users in a run, we recommend chunked upserts of 500 and exponential backoff. We will set a pilot rate-limit exemption for a single-day import (coordinate exact windows).

- Rollout gating: minimum pass criteria for cutover: SAML login success for 5 pilot users from each office region; SCIM sync of user attributes with no >1% error rate; smoke test of API call latency under expected load.

Related items: Jira INF-4821 will track the SCIM rollout tasks; HubSpot deal GLX-2025-0912 updated with the handshake notes.

Will bring these points to the Thursday call and can attach a one-page runbook.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
